newsitem.title: USA: Trade gap still pressuring dlr/yen--Goldman exec.
newsitem.headline: Trade gap still pressuring dlr/yen--Goldman exec.

text.p: Goldman, Sachs (International) vice chairman Robert Hormats applauded U.S.-Japan joint efforts to bolster dollar/yen over the past several months, but warned the dollar may come under pressure.

Speaking to a Columbia Business School conference here, Hormats said, "I think that deal (U.S. and Japan cooperation) has been worked out very successfully. The question is, can it be sustained...in light of what appears to be growing American current account deficits, which are going to lead to pressure on the exchange rate."

Hormats said the persistent U.S.-Japan trade gap and the ensuing excess of dollars in foreign exchange markets threatens to force the dollar lower and test the strength of the bilateral agreement to support the dollar.

Despite the dollar's current strength, having rallied as much as 44 percent from a post-World War II low in 1995, the current account deficit could convince market players that the rally is not sustainable, Hormats added.
The dollar late Friday stood at 111.25 yen. It bottomed out at 79.75 on April 15, 1995.
